title: Kotopoulo Lemonato
subtitle: Greek lemon chicken braised with potatoes
excerpt: Bone-in chicken pieces cooked low and slow in a generous amount of lemon juice, white wine, and olive oil with potatoes. The sauce reduces to something almost syrupy. A Greek Sunday dish that is very simple to make.
sourceNotes: Greek home cooking. Lemonato simply means cooked with lemon. The dish is eaten throughout Greece, often on a Sunday.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dish reheats well. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2 days and the flavour deepens.

content.text: Kotopoulo lemonato works because a lot of lemon juice and olive oil braise together into a glossy, rounded sauce. Do not be tempted to cut back on either. The potatoes cook in the same liquid and soak up all the flavour.
Heat the oven to 180C. Season the chicken pieces all over with salt and black pepper.
Arrange the potato wedges in the roasting tin. Nestle the chicken pieces skin-side up on top of and among the potatoes.
Whisk together the lemon juice, white wine, olive oil, garlic, and oregano. Pour this over the chicken and potatoes. Tuck the thyme sprigs in.
Pour the stock into the base of the tin. Cover tightly with foil and bake for 60 minutes.
Remove the foil. Baste the chicken and potatoes with the pan juices. Return to the oven uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes until the chicken skin is golden and the potatoes are tender.
Rest for 10 minutes. Serve with the pan juices spooned over.

items.cause: The lemon flavour did not mellow during braising.
items.fix: Make sure the foil is sealed and the dish braises rather than evaporates. A long covered cook rounds out the lemon.

items.cause: The wedges were cut too thick or were placed under the chicken and didn't get enough heat.
items.fix: Cut wedges no more than 4cm and make sure they are not buried at the bottom with no contact with the liquid.

items.cause: Foil was left on too long.
items.fix: Remove the foil for the last 25 minutes and baste well. If still pale, give it 5 more minutes under the grill.
